verdict.line: You lose trades before level 3 or whenever you fight outside your own Hallowed Mist; you win every exchange you force inside it.

brief.thesis: W (Hallowed Mist) can only be entered — not shot into — so Teemo must physically walk into your mist to land Q (Blinding Dart) or auto-attack you with E (Toxic Shot) stacks, which strips him of his entire ranged poke kit the moment you drop it. That single interaction, not raw damage, is why the head-to-head sits flat at 50% over 500 games: lane is decided by who controls when the mist goes up, not by outdamaging his poison.

theirWindow.when: W is down and you're within 680 range
theirWindow.what: Blinding Dart has no skillshot to dodge and no bonus cooldown reduction (flat 8s), so he will poke on cooldown — back out past 680 range or trade immediately rather than soaking it for free.

yourWindow.when: W is up and he steps into the mist
yourWindow.what: The instant he enters to Q or auto you, dash in with E (Skip 'n Slash) for the attack speed/range/on-hit window, then Q (Snip Snip!) for the true-damage center hit — he has no dash or blind-immunity to answer a mist all-in.

start.why: AP and sustain to eat early Toxic Shot stacks while you wait for W to come online at level 3.

boots.why: Every point of his damage (Q, E, R) is magic, and this choice measures higher at 50.9% over 231 games versus Sorcerer's Shoes.

core.why: Scales your mist all-ins with raw AP first, the most-run path at 55.3% win rate over 152 games.
Bonus burst damage against the low-HP targets your passive (A Thousand Cuts) already punishes.
Converts your snowball from mist skirmishes into lethal R (Needlework) poke range.

situational.when: you're ahead early and want to burst harder off E (Skip 'n Slash) resets
lane drags into extended skirmishes and you need omnivamp through his poison
his R traps or a jungler threaten to punish your mist dives
you're leaning on E auto-resets rather than burst combos

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the exact pattern this lane runs on — baiting him into your mist and landing the first hit — with bonus gold and damage, and it measures the highest win rate of the available pages at 52.1%.

summoners.why: Most-played and best-performing combo at 50.3% over 54.2% pick rate — Ignite punishes the trades you force once he's forced to enter your mist, where his only defensive tool is Camouflage, which requires standing still and doing nothing.

playing.title: Hold W, don't preemptively mist
playing.detail: Popping Hallowed Mist too early just tells him to back off; wait until he commits to a poke attempt or you're ready to engage.

playing.title: Track the 8-second Q timer
playing.detail: Blinding Dart has no rank scaling on cooldown, so once he fires it you have a full 8 seconds of guaranteed safe trading or shoving.

playing.title: Dash in only inside your mist
playing.detail: E (Skip 'n Slash) outside the mist just exposes you to his auto-attack poison stacks with no protection.

playing.title: Respect Camouflage near brush
playing.detail: If he stands still for a moment he vanishes; don't push blind into unwarded grush expecting to see him coming.

playing.title: Play around traps from level 6
playing.detail: Noxious Trap has only a 1-second cooldown per cast, so he can carpet an area fast — don't dive through grass without vision.

playing.title: Snowball mist all-ins into items
playing.detail: Once Dusk and Dawn and Shadowflame are online, the same mist trade pattern starts ending in kills, not just chip damage.

playing.title: Threaten with R at 1200 range
playing.detail: Needlework punishes any overextension past level 6, but its base cooldown is 120/100/80s pre-rank-4, so don't throw it away on a non-kill.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mist-control reading of the matchup is my own tactical analysis layered on top.
